security_audit.summary: All 76 static findings are false positives involving Markdown, reference URLs, model-selection advice, or documented token storage. One semantic concern remains: the shell-injection safety claim overlooks unsafe shell interpolation of user-controlled JSON. No evidence found of malicious instructions or credential exfiltration; external CLI behavior was not independently verified.

remediation.issue: The shell-injection safety claim ignores shell parsing before the CLI receives input.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the absolute safety claim and require argument-array execution or shell-safe quoting of serialized JSON containing user-provided URLs and prompts.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Safety Claim Omits Host-Shell Quoting
semantic_findings.description: The claim "No shell-injection surface" overlooks shell parsing before CLI execution. Directly inserting user-controlled JSON into the demonstrated single-quoted argument can permit command injection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples use single-quoted JSON while the safety claim only addresses CLI expansion. Exploitation depends on unsafe interpolation; no executable vulnerable wrapper is supplied.

content.value_statement: Lip-sync workflows require different models for existing videos, portraits, and scripts. This skill selects a suitable RunComfy route and prepares the corresponding CLI workflow.
actual_capabilities: Select models by input type, quality requirements, and budget.
Prepare Sync Labs sync v2 or Pro commands for existing video and audio.
Prepare OmniHuman commands for portrait and audio inputs.
Recommend script-based generation routes when no audio file is available.
Explain source preparation, output downloads, and documented CLI exit codes.
limitations: Requires the external RunComfy CLI, authentication, and access to the hosted service.
Script-based routes are recommendations; complete invocation examples cover only video-plus-audio and portrait-plus-audio workflows.
Consent checks are operator responsibilities, not enforced input gates.
Model availability, pricing, output quality, and external CLI security claims are not independently verified by this skill.

use_cases.title: Localize an Existing Video
use_cases.description: Pair an authorized source video with translated voiceover and choose the appropriate Sync Labs tier.

use_cases.title: Animate a Presenter Portrait
use_cases.description: Use an approved portrait and voice recording to prepare an OmniHuman presenter workflow.

use_cases.title: Choose a Script-Based Route
use_cases.description: Compare documented generation routes for an original script when no recorded voiceover is available.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Lip-Sync Model
prompt_templates.prompt: I have an authorized video and voiceover recording. Recommend the simplest lip-sync route and list the required inputs without running anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: identify the correct input route.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Talking Portrait
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an OmniHuman workflow using [portrait URL] and [audio URL]. Confirm face and voice consent, and show the invocation before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Premium Video Dub
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [video URL] and [translated audio URL] for a consented premium dub. Check duration alignment and prepare Sync Labs Pro arguments.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: plan a higher-quality existing-video dub.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multilingual Production
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan separate OmniHuman jobs for [portrait URL] and [audio URL list]. Confirm consent, safely serialize inputs, and separate outputs. Request approval before execution.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate repeated multilingual jobs with explicit execution approval.

best_practices: Confirm permission for both the face and voice before sending assets to an external generation service.
Use clean voice recordings and align audio duration with the source video.
Pass serialized JSON as a literal argument through an argument-array API or apply shell-safe quoting.
anti_patterns: Using a real person's face or voice without permission.
Choosing script-generated speech when exact synchronization to an existing recording is required.
Inserting untrusted prompts or URLs directly into shell command text.

faq.question: Which model should I use for an existing video?
faq.answer: The skill recommends Sync Labs sync v2 for drafts and Pro for premium delivery. Kling and Creatify are alternative routes.

faq.question: Can I start with a single portrait?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented OmniHuman route accepts a portrait URL and an audio URL.

faq.question: Can I generate speech from a script?
faq.answer: The skill recommends Kling text-to-video lipsync or HappyHorse. Check current model documentation because complete script-route commands are not included.

faq.question: Does the skill run locally?
faq.answer: The CLI runs locally, but generation uses RunComfy's hosted Model API. Authentication and network access are required.

faq.question: Does the skill enforce consent automatically?
faq.answer: No. It instructs operators to confirm face and voice consent, but does not implement an input gate.

faq.question: How are results saved?
faq.answer: The documented workflow downloads supported RunComfy result URLs into the output directory selected through the CLI.
